case_title: Mahadevappa v. State of Karnataka rep. by Public Prosecutor
accused_occupation: Police constable (posted at Police Station, Kaladagi)
weapon: Kerosene oil (poured on the victim and ignited); no separate weapon mentioned
evidence_type: Ocular testimony of family and relative witnesses; medical (post-mortem and doctor's evidence); forensic (FSL report and kerosene bottle recovery); circumstantial; victim's oral statements to father before death
aggravating_circumstances: Repeated demands for money, ill-treatment and assault over the marriage; death by burning within seven years of marriage; accused alone present at the time
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of all charges (ss.498-A and 302 IPC) on 31.05.2000
high_court_outcome: State's appeal allowed; acquittal reversed; convicted under ss.498-A and 302 IPC; sentenced to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Cruelty/dowry-related offence under s.498-A IPC and murder under s.302 IPC
neutral_facts: The victim, a woman married to the accused in June 1994, died in October 1995 from severe burn injuries, about seventeen months after the marriage. The accused, a police constable, lived with her at his posting. Over the marriage the accused was said to drink alcohol heavily, often arriving at the victim's parents' house drunk, and repeatedly demanded money from the victim and her parents, at one stage insisting she bring several thousand rupees from her family. He also beat and ill-treated the victim, including while intoxicated. The victim's father and mother, a brother-in-law and a relative each described these incidents in evidence, saying the victim had complained to them and that her parents had sent money on two occasions. The victim also wrote a letter to her father describing ill-treatment. When the victim's mother and a sister-in-law visited the accused's house, the accused allegedly abused them and beat them with shoes. On the day of the incident, around 8 a.m., only the victim and the accused were in the house. Evidence showed that the victim had been doused with kerosene and set alight in the kitchen, and a bottle of kerosene lay in the room. Broken bangles were found in the room. The post-mortem and forensic reports showed kerosene on the body and burns heavier on the upper body, including a burnt blouse. The accused's explanation was that the victim's nylon sari caught fire accidentally while she was boiling water on the oven. At the hospital the victim told her father that the accused had poured kerosene on her and set her on fire, and she died that evening. The father lodged a complaint the same day. The investigating officer recorded statements, arranged the post-mortem, obtained the forensic report and filed a charge-sheet.
physical_harm: Death from severe burn injuries after the victim was doused with kerosene and set on fire
financial_property_loss: Rs.2,000 sent to the accused by the victim's father (per father's testimony); further demands of Rs.4,000-5,000 not met
motive: Repeated demands for money from the victim and her parents, which the court accepted
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent evidence of the victim's father (PW-1), mother (PW-4), brother-in-law (PW-5) and relative (PW-17) on cruelty and demands; post-mortem and FSL reports; doctor's evidence (PW-6); kerosene bottle in room; broken bangles; kerosene smell on body; burns concentrated on upper body
witness_credibility: Four witnesses found consistent on material issues despite lengthy cross-examination; parents held to be the most natural and material witnesses with no reason to lie
trial_duration: offence: 02.10.1995; trial judgment: 31.05.2000; High Court: 03.01.2007; Supreme Court: 07.01.2019
legal_representation: Accused: Mallikarjun S. Mylar, Manjunath, Ms. Umme Salma, Ms. E. R. Sumathy (Advs.). State: Joseph Aristotle S., Mrs. Priya Aristotle, Shiva P., Ms. Aruna Hannah Dutta, Ms. Anitha Shenoy (Advs.)
investigation_status: FIR registered same day; statements recorded; post-mortem and FSL report obtained; charge-sheet filed; case committed to Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions Judge, 31.05.2000): acquitted. High Court (03.01.2007): acquittal reversed, convicted under ss.498-A and 302 IPC, life imprisonment. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld
prosecution_argument: State argued the Sessions Judge failed to appreciate the evidence and that the High Court rightly found both dowry demand and murder proved
defence_argument: No case for reversal of acquittal and the Sessions Judge's view should be restored; the death was accidental (sari caught fire while boiling water on oven); witnesses turned hostile so the prosecution case should be discarded
legal_principle_applied: Cruelty under s.498-A (Explanations (a) and (b)) assessed from evidence of repeated harassment and demands; homicidal versus accidental death decided on circumstantial evidence and absence of plausible explanation; hostile witnesses do not affect case where other evidence proves it
judicial_aggravating_factors: Repeated cruelty and demands for money from the start of the marriage; death by burning within seven years of marriage; accused was the only person present with no plausible explanation
